messages.author: 22dc0d80dd88c700
messages.subject: recordTable removing duplicates
parts:
Hi, I'm running the recordTable function to extract the camera name from image metadata. I have my images in folders by station name (e.g., AK01), for which there are 20 stations in a higher level folder labeled with the state abbreviation (e.g., AK). The code looks like this:

raw_image_directory <- 'Z:/HeathLab/American Kestrel projects/2017 year-round AMKE study/Renamed_nest_box_images'

raw_images <- file.path(raw_image_directory)

exifTagNames(inDir = raw_images, returnMetadata = FALSE)

rec.db.species.metadata1 <- recordTable(inDir = raw_images,
                                         IDfrom = "directory",
                                         additionalMetadataTags = c("EXIF:ImageDescription", "File:FileName"))

The goal is to make sure that images from SD cards were placed in the proper folder, and that the folder name of each image matches the name of the station that is stored in the metadata. When I run the code, I get a message saying that there are duplicate records:

Warning: timeZone is not specified. Assuming UTC
AK : 11311 images
AK: removed 967 duplicate records

Is this function actually removing duplicate photos? I'm actually surprised that there are duplicate photos in the first place, so I was wondering if anyone has an idea of what's happening when I run this function.

Thanks,

Jay

messages.author: c1310ae8b03a4683
messages.subject: Re: recordTable removing duplicates
parts:
Jay

My Reconyx camera nominally take a picture one per second at the fastest rate. But in practice they can and do take images with the same timestamp within one second. These are defined as duplicate records by camptrapR - and in that they have an identical time stamp, they are duplicates.  The images are not discarded but these records (rows) in the recordable are not included in the recordTable.  There is an argument for the recordTable function that be set to retain these records.  In my case they occur with the camera set to take 3, 5, 10 images for a single trigger (motion) as Reconyx calls this performance - they run at about 5-10% of the total. 

I have accepted them as duplicates - for when I cull the records to to get independent records it needs 3- 60 minutes or longer to get independent records, so records at one second resolution are redundant. But of course if your questions relate to behaviour at one second time scale you may rightly need to retain such records.

David

messages.author: 22dc0d80dd88c700
messages.subject: Re: recordTable removing duplicates
parts: Thanks David, that makes sense that they are just removed from the record table. Our cameras are on a timelapse setting, but they seem to take two images at once sometimes.
